Transmission a utility builds for its own reliability, ageing-equipment or local service needs rather than to solve a regional problem the grid operator identified. It enters the regional plan without the competitive window or the benefit-cost test that regional projects face, which is why consumer advocates treat it as the least-reviewed large category of utility spending.

The assemblies of breakers, switches, and protective relays that route power and isolate faults at a substation or in a power room. It is where the electrical system decides which circuits go dark when something fails — and, built into factory-tested skids, it is how much of a data center's power room now arrives on site.

How many times a second a switching converter turns on and off. A higher frequency lets the inductors, transformers and capacitors that smooth the output shrink in proportion, at the cost of more switching loss — the trade that wide-bandgap semiconductors and soft switching exist to improve.

Matching a generator's voltage, frequency, phase angle and phase rotation to a live bus before its breaker closes. Close out of step and the machine takes a torque shock and a current surge; the synchronizer or sync-check relay exists to make that impossible.

A large generator spinning in synchronism with the grid with no fuel and no turbine — it produces no energy, but supplies inertia, reactive power, and fault current on demand. Retired coal and gas units are being converted into them, keeping the machine and its interconnection alive to stabilize the grid that replaced it.

An AC machine whose rotor turns in exact step with the grid frequency — 1,500 or 1,800 rpm for a four-pole machine at 50 or 60 Hz — carrying a magnetic field set by its excitation. Driven one way it is a motor, the other way a generator; in a rotary UPS it does both, and because its output is made by a spinning magnet rather than by switching, the waveform is inherently a sine wave.

The engineering study a utility runs before connecting a large new load or generator: what the request does to the network, which transformers, lines and substations it overloads, and what upgrades are needed. It follows a feasibility screen and precedes a facilities study that prices those upgrades — and each study is valid only against the grid as modelled that day, which is why the date moves.

A Texas mechanism from a 2023 statute under which a wires utility files a multi-year plan of hardening, wildfire-mitigation, flood and cyber investments for commission approval, then recovers the approved cost through a rider. It moves a class of spending out of the contested rate case and into a pre-approved program.

A contract in which the buyer pays for a committed quantity whether or not it is used. It shifts utilization risk to the buyer and turns a speculative revenue line into one lenders will underwrite — the structure behind both colocation leases and the minimum-take terms in large-load utility tariffs.

The ability, created by the 2022 US climate law, to sell clean-energy tax credits for cash to an unrelated party rather than monetizing them through a tax-equity partnership. It turns credits into a near-cash financing source for utilities with limited tax appetite, usually at a discount to face value that the seller must account for.

Transmission cost of service: the revenue requirement a transmission owner is allowed to collect for its wires, set by the commission and, in ERCOT, recovered from every distribution utility on a postage-stamp basis through a wholesale transmission rate. It can be updated between full rate cases as new lines enter service, so a wires utility's transmission build shows up on bills within months.

Transmission and distribution utility: in a restructured market such as Texas, the regulated company that owns only the wires — poles, lines, substations, meters — and earns its return on that rate base. It owns no generation and sells no energy; retail providers buy delivery from it, and the commission sets its rates. Oncor, CenterPoint and AEP Texas are the pattern.

The twelve-month period of actual costs and sales a rate case uses as its base. A historic test year uses costs already incurred; a forecast or future test year projects them forward. The choice matters: a utility investing faster than it depreciates recovers less under a historic year, which is why commissions sometimes impose one as a discipline.

How hard it is for heat to escape from a part to the air or liquid that carries it away, measured as temperature rise per watt. A converter's current rating is really a thermal statement: the current it can carry before its junction temperature reaches the limit through the path it has been given.

A self-accelerating overheating reaction inside a battery cell: heat triggers reactions that release more heat, potentially propagating cell to cell. The failure mode BESS safety standards are designed to contain.

The strictest US EPA emission stage for diesel engines, cutting nitrogen oxides and particulates to a small fraction of earlier stages, usually with after-treatment such as SCR and a particulate filter. Emergency-only stationary engines are held to an earlier stage; a diesel that will run for prime power, peak shaving or demand response generally must meet it — the regulatory fork in a data center's generator strategy.
A storage contract where the offtaker pays a fixed fee for the right to charge and discharge the battery as they wish — the owner operates the asset, the toller takes the market risk.

The interval between the normal supply failing and the load being carried by the alternate source — sensing, engine start and stabilization, then the switch itself. Stored energy must cover all of it; the standards fix the outer bound and the design decides how much shorter it actually is.

A device that changes AC voltage through two magnetically coupled windings, stepping transmission voltage down through substation, medium-voltage, and unit tiers until equipment can use it. Every step costs a little efficiency, a data-center power chain passes through several, and the lead time on large units is one of the buildout's hardest constraints.
The test method that characterizes how battery fires start and propagate at cell, module, unit, and installation level. Its data feeds fire-safety design and permitting for storage projects.

Uninterruptible power supply: a power stage backed by stored energy — a battery string or a spinning flywheel — that carries the load through grid disturbances until generators start. In data centers it sits between utility power and the IT load.

The Uptime Institute's availability ladder for data centers: Tier I basic, Tier II redundant components, Tier III concurrently maintainable — any part serviceable without downtime — and Tier IV fault-tolerant, surviving any single failure. It is the shorthand buyers use for how much redundancy, and how much capital, a facility carries.

The Virginia Clean Economy Act of 2020: the state law that sets Dominion Energy Virginia on a path to carbon-free generation by 2045 and mandates specific gigawatts of solar, offshore wind and energy storage along the way, executed through annual filings the commission approves. It is the statutory reason the utility runs a standing storage procurement.

Mounting the final converters directly beneath the processor package, on the far side of the board, so current flows straight up through the board into the chip instead of sideways across it. The shorter path cuts resistive loss and frees the board area around the package for signal connections.

A utility that owns generation, transmission and distribution and sells to the end customer under one regulated franchise — Dominion Energy Virginia, Georgia Power and Entergy are the pattern. Contrast a wires-only utility in a restructured market such as Texas, which delivers power it does not generate. Which kind sits across the table decides whether the utility buys plants or only substations.

A control mode that makes a grid-forming inverter behave like a traditional spinning generator, resisting frequency change as though it had rotating mass it does not have. It is how an inverter-based plant supplies the stabilizing behavior retiring thermal plants used to provide for free, and it is what makes black start and off-grid running possible.

Holding a converter's output voltage steady as its input voltage and its load change. A regulated converter watches its output and corrects continuously; an unregulated one simply follows its input by a fixed ratio, trading precision for efficiency and relying on regulation elsewhere in the chain.

Valve-regulated lead-acid: the sealed lead-acid battery that backed data-center UPS for decades — cheap per kilowatt for a few minutes of runtime, but heavy, sensitive to heat, good for only a few hundred deep cycles and replaced every few years. Lithium-ion has been displacing it in new UPS installations on life and footprint.

Voltage regulator module: the last conversion stage on the server board, stepping the rack's supply down to roughly one volt at the processor die. It is the final link in a chain of conversions running from the transmission line to the chip, and every one of them costs efficiency.

A utility's exposure to damages when its equipment starts a wildfire — the largest tail risk in the western US since the California fires, and the reason mitigation plans, public-safety shutoffs and liability legislation now sit in rate cases. Where a state caps or funds the liability the utility's cost of capital falls; where it does not, every dry, windy day is a balance-sheet event.

The commission-reviewed program a utility runs to keep its lines from starting fires and to limit the damage if they do: undergrounding and covered conductor in high-risk zones, faster-acting protection settings, vegetation clearance, weather stations and cameras, and the rules for shutting off power in dangerous wind. Its cost is recovered through a rider and its adequacy is argued in the liability case after the fire.

Water usage effectiveness: water consumed per unit of IT energy, the cooling counterpart to PUE. Closed-loop and air-cooled designs spend a little more electricity to spend almost no water, which in a water-stressed watershed is usually the more permittable trade.

The instant an alternating waveform passes through zero volts, twice per cycle. For a fraction of a millisecond nothing sustains an arc, so an arc drawn on AC tends to extinguish itself — and almost every protective device in an AC building quietly relies on that. Direct current never offers the instant, which is why DC protection has to be engineered rather than inherited.
